{"id": "13513aa3-d6fe-476a-a639-bbd0d24156f8", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "We're about to merge PR #14 in acme/payments-infra. It's the first infrastructure PR in that repo, there's no pipeline review set up, and finance wants to know what this stack is going to add to the AWS bill every month before we approve it. Can you work that out from the PR?

The attached material is what the repository integration and the AWS tools returned for this change. It is a synthetic test fixture: resource names, account results, SKUs and rates are made up, and the rates intentionally differ from real AWS list prices, so treat the rows below as the live lookup results for this run.

--- PR #14 (feature/ledger -> main) ---
Base branch main: no cloudformation/ directory.
Files added: cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml

--- .github/workflows/deploy.yml (excerpt) ---
env:
  AWS_REGION: eu-west-1
  STACK_NAME: payments-ledger
run: aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name payments-ledger --template-file cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml --region eu-west-1

--- cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml (Resources; Parameters hold only VPC and subnet IDs) ---
  LedgerDbSubnetGroup: {Type: AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup, Properties: {SubnetIds: [!Ref PrivateSubnetA, !Ref PrivateSubnetB]}}
  LedgerDb:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties: {Engine: postgres, DBInstanceClass: db.r6g.large, MultiAZ: true, AllocatedStorage: "200", StorageType: gp3, DBSubnetGroupName: !Ref LedgerDbSubnetGroup}
  ReconcilerNatEip: {Type: AWS::EC2::EIP, Properties: {Domain: vpc}}
  ReconcilerNatGateway: {Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway, Properties: {AllocationId: !GetAtt ReconcilerNatEip.AllocationId, SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetA}}
  AlbSecurityGroup: {Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup}
  ApiLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties: {Type: application, Scheme: internet-facing, Subnets: [!Ref PublicSubnetA, !Ref PublicSubnetB], SecurityGroups: [!Ref AlbSecurityGroup]}
  ArchiveBucket: {Type: AWS::S3::Bucket, Properties: {VersioningConfiguration: {Status: Enabled}}}
  ReconcilerRole: {Type: AWS::IAM::Role}
  ReconcilerFunction: {Type: AWS::Lambda::Function, Properties: {Runtime: python3.12, Architectures: [arm64], MemorySize: 512, Role: !GetAtt ReconcilerRole.Arn}}

--- AWS (read-only), eu-west-1 ---
cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name payments-ledger
  -> ValidationError: Stack with id payments-ledger does not exist

--- pricing get-products (endpoint us-east-1, filter regionCode=eu-west-1), OnDemand terms only ---
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-01  usagetype EU-Multi-AZUsage:db.r6g.large   databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.500 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-09  usagetype EU-UnusedBox:db.r6g.large       databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.000 USD per Hrs   "unused capacity reservation hour"
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-02  usagetype EU-RDS:Multi-AZ-GP3-Storage     volumeType=General Purpose-GP3 databaseEngine=PostgreSQL   0.250 USD per GB-Mo
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-01  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Hours             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per Hrs
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-02  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Bytes             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per GB
AmazonVPC  SKU FX-IP-01   usagetype EU-PublicIPv4:InUseAddress                                  0.005 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-01  usagetype EU-LoadBalancerUsage            productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.025 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-03  usagetype EU-TS-LoadBalancerUsage         productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.006 USD per Hrs   "trust store unit-hour"
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-02  usagetype EU-LCUUsage                     productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.008 USD per LCU-Hrs", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "82c866da-60f9-4562-a5db-0988af2c194c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Estimate monthly AWS costs for PR #14 infrastructure"}]}

{"id": "6e45a2f1-7b94-410e-8470-63e87a5026d8", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is a bounded calculation I can do directly from the fixture data rather than delegating, so I'm working through monthly cost estimates for each billable resource in the PR, starting with LedgerDb's RDS compute and storage costs at the given hourly rate.

RDS totals out to $415/mo combining compute and storage, while the unused capacity reservation is $0 and irrelevant. Moving to the NAT gateway and EIP, I'm calculating hourly charges but flagging data processing as variable since it depends on usage volume. For the ALB, the hourly rate is straightforward but LCU-based charges are usage-dependent and can't be pinned down without traffic data.

The trust store SKU doesn't apply since the template has no mTLS configuration, so I'll exclude that cost entirely. For the S3 archive bucket and Lambda function, there's no pricing SKU provided in the fixture, so both need to be flagged as unavailable for cost calculation since they're usage-based anyway.

I'm now summing the fixed, predictable recurring monthly charges for resources running continuously: RDS compute at $365, RDS storage at $50, NAT Gateway hours at $36.50, the attached EIP at $3.65, and ALB hours at $18.25, while the IAM role, security group, and subnet group contribute nothing since they're free.

That totals $473.40/mo as the baseline, leaving several usage-dependent costs uncomputed without traffic data—NAT Gateway data processing, ALB LCU usage, S3 storage/requests, and Lambda invocations all lack enough information or depend on actual volume. I also note the FX-RDS-09 unused capacity reservation line is priced at $0.000/hr, so it's zero-rated and doesn't affect the total.

I'll skip the ALB Trust Store line since no mutual TLS is configured, and I'll stick with the standard 730 hours/month convention. Since this is all fixture data already provided rather than something requiring live lookups, I can just compute the breakdown directly: a fixed baseline run-rate around $473/month, an itemized list, and a clear note on which costs remain usage-dependent and can't be calculated without traffic assumptions.

No need to offer an investigation path here since this isn't an unknown-cause problem. I'll just answer directly, laying out the cost breakdown clearly, probably with a table.

"}]}

{"id": "6d32520a-051c-4e68-a178-309bbd7c9a71", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the monthly run-rate for the `payments-ledger` stack, based on the pricing rows pulled for `eu-west-1` and assuming 730 hrs/month (standard AWS convention) for anything billed 24/7:

**Fixed baseline — resources that run continuously regardless of traffic**

| Resource | Rate | Monthly | 
|---|---|---|
| RDS `db.r6g.large`, Multi-AZ compute | $0.500/hr | **$365.00** |
| RDS GP3 storage, 200 GB Multi-AZ | $0.250/GB-mo | **$50.00** |
| NAT Gateway hours | $0.050/hr | **$36.50** |
| EIP (in-use, attached to NAT GW) | $0.005/hr | **$3.65** |
| ALB hours | $0.025/hr | **$18.25** |
| **Baseline total** | | **≈ $473.40/mo** |

**Not a cost in this fixture:**
- The RDS "unused capacity reservation" line (`FX-RDS-09`) is rated at $0.000/hr — zero-rated, no impact.
- The ALB trust-store line (`FX-ALB-03`) only applies if mutual-TLS trust store is configured on the listener — the template doesn't set one up, so it doesn't apply here.

**Usage-dependent — can't be pinned to a number without traffic/volume assumptions:**
- NAT Gateway data processing ($0.050/GB) — scales with egress through the reconciler's NAT path.
- ALB LCU-hours ($0.008/LCU-hr) — scales with connections, bandwidth, and rule evaluations.
- `ArchiveBucket` (S3) — no pricing row was returned for S3 in this lookup, and it's storage/request-volume-dependent regardless.
- `ReconcilerFunction` (Lambda, arm64, 512MB) — no pricing row returned; serverless billing is invocation/duration-based, typically negligible until the reconciler runs frequently.

So the number to give finance is: **~$473/month fixed, plus variable NAT data transfer, ALB LCU usage, S3, and Lambda costs that scale with traffic/invocation volume.** If you can give me an expected request rate or data egress estimate for the reconciler, I can turn the variable piece into a number too.

One more thing worth flagging since you mentioned it: this is Multi-AZ RDS + NAT + internet-facing ALB for what looks like a first infra PR with no pipeline review — worth double-checking Multi-AZ is intentional, since dropping to Single-AZ would roughly halve the RDS compute line.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
